ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The doubled command tells someone to rest, cease, and settle; later speakers quote it, criticize fixed adherence to it, or refuse both it and its negation.
EvidenceBody: Chan records preserve it both as Shishuang Qingzhu's compact sequence of stilling images and as a disputed formula: Yunfeng Wenyue reverses it, Yulin Tongxiu refuses both alternatives, and Dahui Zonggao and Zhongfeng Mingben criticize inert or formulaic applications. Shishuang Qingzhu's recorded sequence expands it: "rest; cease; let one thought last ten thousand years; become cold ashes and a withered tree; become an incense burner in an old shrine; become one strip of white silk; become cold and still" (休去歇去、一念萬年去、寒灰枯木去、古廟香爐去、一條白練去、冷秋秋地去). Yunfeng Wenyue supplies a contrary sequence beginning "do not rest and do not cease" (不休不歇去), and Yulin Tongxiu says that neither resting-and-ceasing nor not-resting-and-not-ceasing is permitted (也不許休去歇去，也不許不休不歇去). Dahui Zonggao reports people sitting slack-jawed and calling that "resting and ceasing" (一向嘴盧都地打坐，謂之休去歇去), in an extended criticism. Zhongfeng Mingben likewise reports people citing "do not fantasize, put it down, old-shrine incense burner, rest and cease" as evidence, and compares that use to waiting by a stump for a rabbit. Other records retain the literal instruction: Yunmen Wenyan says, "from now on, rest; cease" (自今以往，休去歇去), while Dafang Yin asks, "why not rest and cease?" (何不休去歇去). The entry records the command, its stock sequence, its contrary, and the corpus's criticisms; it does not turn the words into a prescribed system.
